raw_case_text:
A 70-year-old female patient diagnosed with Philadelphia-like CRLF2 overexpression B-cell precursor ALL was admitted to our hospital in 2021. She underwent induction chemotherapy of the VDLD regimen (vindesine, idarubicin, dexamethasone, and pegylated asparaginase) on August 1, 2021, and achieved complete remission. However, she experienced complications of chemotherapy-induced bone marrow suppression, febrile neutropenia, and bloodstream infection of Pseudomonas aeruginosa. Treatment with granulocyte colony-stimulating factor and meropenem led to complete recovery by August 21. Her past medical history included hypertension and steroid-induced diabetes, both of which recovered after induction chemotherapy. Additionally, she underwent cholecystectomy due to cholecystolithiasis and thyroid nodulectomy with normal thyroid function.
For consolidation therapy following prior induction chemotherapy, she received blinatumomab on September 10th (9 mug per day during the first week and 28 mug per day during the next 3 weeks) via continuous infusion. Her white blood cell (WBC) count was 9.84 x 109/L, and the lymphocyte count was 1.55 x 109/L on September 8th. On the second day of blinatumomab infusion, she presented with subfebrile fever, which was thought attributed to mild cytokine release syndrome (CRS) and managed with loxoprofen. The WBC and lymphocyte count were 10.9 x 109/L and 0.91 x 109/L on September 10, separately. However, on the 9th day after blinatumomab use, she experienced intermittent fever without obvious respiratory symptoms, and her WBC count increased to 18.1 x 109/L. Chest CT revealed subtle infiltrates and nodules. The patient received empiric treatment with piperacillin/tazobactam, acyclovir, and 160 mg trimethoprim (TMP)/800 mg sulfamethoxazole (SMX) daily for PCP infection prophylaxis. Despite treatment, the fever persisted, and loxoprofen was administered as needed.
On the 17th day of blinatumomab treatment, she developed obvious shortness of breath, and her pulse oxygen saturation decreased to 78%. Chest CT showed diffuse GGO with scattered small nodules (as shown in Fig. 1). Additionally, her lymphocyte count decreased to 0.59 x 109/L, C-reactive protein increased from 2.41 to 109.75 (reference <3) mg/L, LDH increased from 250 to 413 (reference <250) U/L, and beta-D-glucan assays showed 298.6 (reference <100.5) pg/mL, all indicative of possible PCP infection. The dry cough with no sputum prompted next-generation sequencing of peripheral blood, which tested positive for pneumocystis jirovecii without evidence of other pathogens. Consequently, the patient was diagnosed with PCP.
Therapeutic dosages of TMP-SMX (15 mg/kg/day of the TMP component) and dexamethasone (8 mg IV twice a day for 5 days, gradually tapered over 14 days) were administered, and the first cycle of blinatumomab had to be stopped. She ultimately achieved complete recovery, and an additional four cycles of blinatumomab with prophylaxis of PCP (160 mg TMP/800 mg SMX daily) were administered. As of now, MRD has consistently been negative during follow-ups.

subjective.chief_complaint: A 70-year-old female with Philadelphia-like B-cell precursor acute lymphoblastic leukemia developed intermittent fever on day 9 and acute dyspnea with dry cough on day 17 of continuous blinatumomab consolidation therapy.
subjective.history_of_present_illness: The patient was diagnosed with Philadelphia-like CRLF2-overexpressing B-cell precursor ALL in 2021 and achieved complete remission following VDLD induction chemotherapy (vindesine, idarubicin, dexamethasone, pegylated asparaginase) started on August 1, 2021, which was complicated by febrile neutropenia and Pseudomonas aeruginosa bacteremia that resolved with G-CSF and meropenem by August 21. On September 10, 2021, she started consolidation therapy with continuous intravenous blinatumomab (9 μg/day week 1, then 28 μg/day). She had a subfebrile temperature on day 2 attributed to mild cytokine release syndrome (managed with loxoprofen). On day 9 of blinatumomab, she developed intermittent fever without obvious respiratory symptoms that persisted despite empiric piperacillin/tazobactam, acyclovir, and prophylactic-dose TMP-SMX (160 mg/800 mg daily). On day 17 of blinatumomab, she developed acute shortness of breath and dry cough without sputum.
subjective.past_medical_history: Philadelphia-like CRLF2-overexpressing B-cell precursor ALL in first complete remission; prior chemotherapy-induced febrile neutropenia and Pseudomonas aeruginosa bloodstream infection (August 2021); hypertension and steroid-induced diabetes (both resolved post-induction); status post cholecystectomy for cholecystolithiasis and thyroid nodulectomy (euthyroid).
subjective.review_of_systems: Positive for intermittent fever, acute shortness of breath, and non-productive dry cough.

objective.physical_examination: On day 17 of blinatumomab infusion: Obvious shortness of breath and severe hypoxemia with pulse oxygen saturation (SpO2) dropping to 78%.
objective.routine_investigations: Serial complete blood counts and inflammatory markers: Baseline pre-blinatumomab (September 8) WBC 9.84 x 10^9/L and lymphocytes 1.55 x 10^9/L; day 2 (September 10) WBC 10.9 x 10^9/L and lymphocytes 0.91 x 10^9/L; day 9 WBC rose to 18.1 x 10^9/L; day 17 lymphocyte count fell to 0.59 x 10^9/L, C-reactive protein (CRP) surged from 2.41 to 109.75 mg/L (reference <3 mg/L), and lactate dehydrogenase (LDH) increased from 250 to 413 U/L (reference <250 U/L).
objective.advanced_workup: Serial chest CT scans: Day 9 chest CT showed subtle pulmonary infiltrates and nodules; day 17 chest CT demonstrated diffuse ground-glass opacities (GGO) with scattered small nodules. Fungal biomarker (day 17): Elevated serum 1,3-beta-D-glucan at 298.6 pg/mL (reference <100.5 pg/mL). Peripheral blood metagenomic next-generation sequencing (mNGS): Positive for Pneumocystis jirovecii with no other pathogens detected.

assessment_and_plan.assessment_and_confirmation: Final diagnosis: Pneumocystis jirovecii pneumonia (PCP) during blinatumomab consolidation therapy for B-cell precursor ALL, definitively confirmed by peripheral blood next-generation sequencing (mNGS), elevated serum beta-D-glucan (298.6 pg/mL), elevated LDH (413 U/L), lymphopenia (0.59 x 10^9/L), and diffuse bilateral GGOs on chest CT. Plan and clinical course: The first cycle of blinatumomab was halted, and therapeutic-dose trimethoprim-sulfamethoxazole (TMP-SMX, 15 mg/kg/day of the TMP component) plus intravenous dexamethasone (8 mg IV twice daily for 5 days, tapered over 14 days) were administered. The patient achieved complete clinical and radiographic recovery and subsequently completed four additional consolidation cycles of blinatumomab under daily TMP-SMX prophylaxis (160 mg/800 mg daily), maintaining persistent minimal residual disease (MRD)-negative remission on follow-up.
